testcase.name: components.dns

failure.message: 1 of 1 cluster-DNS pod is in kube-system not ready (Running): in-cluster name resolution is failing or one node outage away from it, and every Dapr call, database connection and object-store request resolves through them

testcase.failure: coredns-1 0/0 Running `kubectl -n kube-system describe pod coredns-1` and `kubectl -n kube-system logs coredns-1` — a CrashLooping CoreDNS is usually a bad Corefile, an unreachable upstream resolver in the node's /etc/resolv.conf, or a forwarding loop back into itself. Fix it before installing; nothing in the ApplicationSets can.

testcase.name: components.ingress

failure.message: no running controller could be matched to the IngressClass (traefik (traefik.io/ingress-controller)): if nothing is serving it, every Ingress the install creates stays unclaimed and no hostname the chart publishes answers

testcase.failure: check the controller is running (`kubectl get pods -A | grep -i ingress`). budctl ties a class to its controller by name, because spec.controller is a vendor identifier with no API link to a workload — so a controller whose pods carry none of those names, or one that runs outside the cluster such as a cloud load-balancer controller, is not matched here, and `domains.inbound-80` / `domains.inbound-443` are what prove that path instead.
